subject: Pathology
summary: The Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT) detects antibodies or complement on a patient’s red cells, guiding diagnosis of autoimmune hemolytic anemia and transfusion reactions. It informs transfusion safety and treatment choices.

sections.p: DAT identifies IgG or complement bound to red blood cells in vivo. A positive result indicates immune-mediated hemolysis or a transfusion reaction.

t.b: Positive = immune hemolysis or transfusion reaction; negative = unlikely immune cause.

sections.p: DAT itself is not staged, but a positive result prompts evaluation of hemolysis severity via hemoglobin, LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin, and reticulocyte count.
b: Mild hemolysis: hemoglobin >10 g/dL, mild LDH elevation

sections.p: The most common causes of a positive DAT are warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia and transfusion reactions. Other causes include cold agglutinin disease, drug-induced hemolysis, and infections.

t.b: Positive DAT with IgG suggests warm AIHA.
Positive DAT with C3d indicates complement-mediated hemolysis.

sections.p: Patients may have fatigue, pallor, jaundice, dark urine, or splenomegaly. Transfusion reactions present with fever, chills, hypotension, or hemoglobinuria.

t.b: Presence of jaundice or hemoglobinuria supports hemolysis.

sections.p: After a positive DAT, confirm hemolysis and identify the specific antibody. In low-resource settings, a simple antibody screen and crossmatch may suffice.

t.b: Identifies specific antibody for transfusion matching.

sections.p: Severe hemolysis can lead to acute kidney injury, disseminated intravascular coagulation, or death. Rapid identification and transfusion avoidance are critical.

whenToSeekHelp: Acute hemolysis with hypotension or renal failure
Severe anemia with rapid drop in hemoglobin

faq.q: What does a positive DAT mean?
faq.a: It shows antibodies or complement attached to red cells, indicating immune hemolysis or a transfusion reaction.

faq.q: Can DAT be negative in hemolytic anemia?
faq.a: Yes, if hemolysis is non-immune or antibodies are below detection limits.

faq.q: Do I need a blood transfusion if DAT is positive?
faq.a: Only if the patient is symptomatic or severely anemic; otherwise treat the underlying cause.

exam: Explain the clinical significance of a positive DAT in a patient with unexplained anemia.
Describe the steps to manage a transfusion reaction when DAT is positive.
Differentiate between warm and cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia based on DAT findings.
